intro.en: Campaigns, votes and results: how an election is told in Spanish.

texto.en:
**Before.** The government **convoca elecciones**: **generales**, **autonómicas** (regional) or **municipales**. The parties choose **un candidato**, write **un programa electoral** and start **la campaña**, with **mítines** and **debates**. **Los sondeos** predict the result. The day before the vote is **la jornada de reflexión**, when campaigning is forbidden.

**The day.** Each **votante** goes to **un colegio electoral**, takes **una papeleta**, puts it in an envelope and drops it in **la urna**. You can also **votar en blanco**, cast **un voto nulo** or **abstenerte**. The percentage of people who vote is **la participación**; the rest is **la abstención**.

**After.** Votes become **escaños**. A party with more than half has **mayoría absoluta**. If nobody has it, the parties **pactan** and form **una coalición**. The others are **la oposición**.

**The chambers.** In Spain, **los diputados** sit in **el Congreso** and **los senadores** in **el Senado**. Together they are **las Cortes**.

**The three powers.** **El poder legislativo**, **el ejecutivo** and **el judicial**.

**Losing power.** A politician **dimite**. A government falls after **una moción de censura**. Power taken by force is **un golpe de Estado**, and what follows is **una dictadura**.

**Verbs with prepositions.** **Votar a** un partido, **presentarse a** las elecciones, **pertenecer a** un partido, **abstenerse de** votar.

frases.es: A las ocho de la tarde cerraron los colegios electorales y empezó una de las noches más largas que se recuerdan.
frases.en: At eight in the evening the polling stations closed and one of the longest nights in memory began.
analisis: A las ocho de la tarde
una de las noches más largas

frases.es: La participación había sido del setenta por ciento, cinco puntos más de lo que anunciaban los sondeos.
frases.en: Turnout had been seventy per cent, five points more than the polls were predicting.
analisis: de lo que anunciaban los sondeos

frases.es: Con la mitad de las papeletas contadas, ningún partido se acercaba a la mayoría absoluta.
frases.en: With half the ballot papers counted, no party was getting close to an absolute majority.
analisis: Con la mitad de las papeletas contadas

frases.es: El candidato del gobierno había perdido veinte escaños, pero seguía siendo el más votado.
frases.en: The government's candidate had lost twenty seats, but was still the one with most votes.

frases.es: Poco antes de medianoche, la líder de la oposición anunció que estaba dispuesta a pactar con cualquiera que respetara su programa.
frases.en: Shortly before midnight, the leader of the opposition announced that she was willing to make a deal with anyone who respected her programme.

frases.es: Nadie dimitió esa noche, aunque más de un diputado se quedó sin escaño.
frases.en: Nobody resigned that night, although more than one member of parliament was left without a seat.

frases.es: Los analistas coinciden en que, a menos que se forme una coalición, habrá que convocar nuevas elecciones antes del verano.
frases.en: Analysts agree that, unless a coalition is formed, new elections will have to be called before the summer.

pregunta.en: According to the text, did any party win an absolute majority?

No.en: Ningún partido se acercaba a la mayoría absoluta.

Yes, the opposition.en: Its leader offered to make deals.

pregunta.en: According to the text, what will happen if no coalition is formed?

The candidate will resign.en: The text does not say that.

The opposition will govern.en: The text does not say that.

pregunta.en: The box where you put your vote is…

el escaño.en: That is a seat in parliament.

pregunta.en: Complete: I always vote for the same party.

por el.en: In Spain the usual form is votar a.

explicacion.en: Dimitir is to resign of one's own will.

bloques.frase: El gobierno ha convocado elecciones para el mes de mayo

traduccion.en: The government has called an election for May.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an analysis of the last elections in your country: results, surprises and consequences.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud why many people do not vote, and whether voting should be compulsory.
